title: Throttle-aware lazy index rewriter to reduce IO spikes for dashboard queries
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Problem: Periodic IO spike events on the Console dashboards are correlated with large tenant scans triggered by index rewrites during background maintenance and first-read hotspots. These spikes increase tail latency for paginated dashboard queries and occasionally breach the 500ms SLO for interactive routes.

Goal: Implement a throttle-aware, lazy index rewriter and request-side hint propagation so that: (1) index maintenance work is rate-limited by tenant and cluster load, (2) expensive rewrites are performed lazily on demand during low-load windows or in small incremental slices, and (3) dashboard query handlers can attach cheap index-hints to avoid full-range scans.

Scope: Backend services that drive query planning and the analytics materialization pipeline. Work touches the query planner, background index maintenance worker, and the dashboard API gateway. Does NOT include UI changes.

Acceptance criteria:
- Reduction of 95th percentile dashboard tail latency during index maintenance windows by >= 40% measured on synthetic workload and production canary region.
- End-to-end benchmarking showing sustained throughput with <10% additional CPU cost for background workers.
- Graceful fallbacks: if lazy rewrites are not possible, queries still return correct results within SLOs via lightweight on-path hedging.

Design proposal summary:
1) Throttle controller: a central, soft-state controller per cluster that exposes dynamic capacity tokens for maintenance ops. Tokens are consumed by background index rewrite jobs; controller adjusts token rate from observed dashboard query latency and queue depth metrics.
2) Lazy rewrite strategy: when an index shard is flagged for rewrite, the background worker will attempt a small, bounded rewrite slice (time-boxed and token-limited). If further work is required, it enqueues follow-ups.
3) Read-side index hints: dashboard query planner will consult a small, in-memory index-summary (bloom + small histogram) to choose between scan, seek, or prefix read. If hint suggests expensive path, the planner attaches a low-cost background rewrite request to the response headers so the maintenance queue can prioritize it opportunistically.
4) Safety & correctness: all lazy rewrites are idempotent; queries receiving incomplete rewrites will fall back to existing scan logic and will be hedged with a short, speculative read to a secondary replica.
5) Telemetry: new metrics - maintenance_token_rate, maintenance_backlog_length, rewrite_slice_duration, hint_hit_ratio, query_scan_rate_during_maintenance. Dashboards and alerting playbooks updated.

Trade-offs considered:
- Doing big rewrites quickly reduces long-term query cost but creates short-term tail spikes. We favor incremental work for predictable latency at the cost of slightly longer stabilization times.
- More aggressive read-time hedging increases short-term cost but preserves UX. Enforcement will be tiered by tenant priority.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 0 (canary): implement telemetry + feature flag for throttle controller in a single cluster. Run for 1 week, compare tail metrics.
- Phase 1 (limited tenants): enable lazy rewrite and hint propagation for low-to-medium traffic tenants with feature flag. Monitor SLOs.
- Phase 2 (gradual ramp): increase tenant percentage and enable token-rate auto-tuning.
- Phase 3 (global): flip default for all tenants, add admin controls in Console to tune per-tenant token budgets.

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests for rate token logic and hint encoding.
- Integration tests simulating concurrent background rewrites + high query load with chaos injection (worker pauses, network jitter).
- Benchmark harness: synthetic tenant workloads (mix of long-range scans and small-selects) run against staging with latency collectors.
- Production canary: dark launch index-hint header and telemetry for 24 hours, then enable lazy rewrites for 5 tenants.

Migration notes:
- Existing index metadata extended with small stable identifier and a lightweight summary blob. Backfill process included to generate summaries for hot shards; backfill itself uses the same throttle controller to avoid storming.

Security & compliance: no change to data residency or encryption. Background workers will continue to respect KMS/HSM and tenant isolation boundaries.
comments: 2025-01-29 - Aisha Khan: Initial triage. Observed correlation between nightly 'index-rewrite' jobs and 99th percentile spikes on dashboard queries in us-west-2. Filed an ops ticket with logs (ops-INC-1421).

2025-02-05 - Jonas Park: Spike reproduction harness created. Found that a full-shard rewrite can introduce 3x CPU and 2x disk IO for up to 30s on a busy host. Pushing design PR for the throttle controller (WIP).

2025-02-18 - Priya Nair (Product): Confirmed customer reports about interactive dashboards timing out during maintenance windows. Prioritizing as P1 for Q1 console improvements. Suggested per-tenant opt-in for early testing.

2025-02-26 - Jonas Park: Implemented maintenance_token_rate metric and slice-limited rewrite worker. Benchmarks in staging show 45% reduction in 95p tail during simulated rewrite windows. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/6821

2025-03-03 - Marco Li (SRE): Ran production canary in canary-cluster-3 with two tenants. Observed token controller correctly throttling work and keeping median latency steady; noted an edge-case where backlog grows under network partitions. Filed follow-up ENG-219002.
2025-03-06 - Jonas Park: Addressed edge-case by adding backlog eviction policy and retry jitter. Preparing for limited tenant rollout next week.
